headline: Last session: Indian benchmark shares fell amid heavy FII selling, recording longest weekly losing run in 25 years.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Massive selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) drove significant market drops.
Rising crude oil prices and global rate hikes triggered continuous foreign capital outflows.
Market volatility prevented benchmark indices like Nifty and Sensex from sustaining intraday recoveries.
Concerns over global macroeconomic conditions continued to depress market sentiment.
whatHappening: Indian equity benchmark indices logged their worst weekly losing run in 25 years.
Markets fell for eight consecutive weeks as investors suffered massive wealth erosion.
Sensex crashed up to 1,000 points in recent sessions, wiping out billions in market capitalisation.
SEBI is evaluating position limits for non-agricultural derivative contracts to improve market liquidity.
summary: Indian benchmark indices closed lower in recent sessions, marking an eight-week losing streak—the longest in 25 years—driven by persistent foreign investor selling. Geopolitical tensions, global rate hikes, and rising oil prices further pressured investor sentiment. The market is closed today for the weekend and will resume trading on Monday, 5 October.
